name: R111 single lookup ablation
status: implementation experiment; accepted runtime remains R109
hypothesis: R110-A adds clients.get_mut before a receive loop that immediately performs the same lookup again. Reuse that first mutable Client borrow for the first read, then reacquire only after Server::receive may have changed client state. This may remove part of the measured +3.1% user instructions versus R109.
change_boundary: Use R110-A stack buffer and exact residual code without changes.
Change only service_client reference lifetime: reuse Client for read/end; reacquire after dispatch, with the same missing-client/disconnect behavior.
No boxed Client table, borrowed dispatch, threshold, inline hint, allocator size or protocol change.
Preserve all R110-A boundary tests. Work in an isolated Git worktree; main branch remains accepted R109.
validation: Compile and run portable boundary tests to validate the borrow structure.
Build at the original canonical path with original release flags; compare exact R110-A control SHA to preserved artifact.
Linux/router correctness and byte-differential gates before any physical timing.
Freeze exact new ELF and synchronized Oracle counter plan after the build; compare R111, R110-A and R109 with fixed permutations at 0/64 held connections.

A successful counter ablation is evidence for source-level extra work, not proof of router improvement. Only then decide the minimal router timing needed; do not repeat the whole six-series matrix for a known memory-failing candidate.
decision: Do not accept this as a final daemon: the unchanged R110-A memory gate is still failed. If instruction inflation is not removed, retain evidence and inspect generated code rather than trying another control-flow variant. A separate client-table ownership experiment needs its own plan and measurements.
